proposedCriteria.title: Proactive legs are enabled by default
proposedCriteria.model: Every registered native code-intelligence push leg is enabled by default.
proposedCriteria.driftMarkers: A registered push leg has a default-OFF flag or lacks an explicit registered flag.
proposedCriteria.method: Read PUSH_LEG_FLAGS and FLAG_DEFAULTS in the exact pinned source. Run push-channel.test.ts through testing:run and retain the case 'keeps every registered leg ON by default'. Its nonempty registered-leg set must be checked against true defaults; a removed leg must be disclosed against D-016. Change one default to false as a controlled negative and require that case to fail. Restore the source before recording the passing run. No source substitution or skipped case counts.

proposedCriteria.title: Push delivery uses the precomputed snapshot
proposedCriteria.model: The shared mid-turn code-intelligence injector serves eligible pushes from the precomputed first-party snapshot without starting or awaiting a cold language server.
proposedCriteria.driftMarkers: An eligible snapshot-backed push starts or waits for a compiler, a missing snapshot initiates a cold compiler, or the bounded delivery wall is exceeded without abandoning the pending delivery.
proposedCriteria.method: Trace codeIntelPushText from PostToolBatch into the snapshot loader and commit seam. Run the bound unit and real-database integration suites through testing:run. Require the available-snapshot positive, cold/missing-snapshot negative and slow-context/abandoned-commit cases to execute. Preserve snapshot source identity, rendered nonempty answer and ledger row in the positive; compiler-start or a late abandoned commit is fail. A missing snapshot must return without compilation. An unexecuted hot-path case is unknown, never pass.

proposedCriteria.title: Pushes obey the shared turn budget
proposedCriteria.model: Code-intelligence pushes remain within the shared per-turn character budget after memory's allocation, including simultaneous worker deliveries.
proposedCriteria.driftMarkers: Memory and code intelligence exceed the shared turn allocation, concurrent deliveries overspend the code-intelligence turn budget, or a dropped oversized fact is clipped into misleading evidence.
proposedCriteria.method: Run the bound suites through testing:run. Require 'delivers immediately from an available snapshot and gives memory its budget first', 'concurrent workers cannot spend the per-turn budget more than once', and whole-fact drop cases. Read the budget writer and retain exact delivered-character sums and memory-reduced request allocation. Concurrent distinct facts must produce nonempty deliveries within CODE_INTEL_PUSH_TURN_CHARS; memory exhaustion must suppress a push. Overspend or partial clipping fails; zero eligible deliveries cannot establish the positive.

proposedCriteria.title: Push facts deduplicate within a session epoch
proposedCriteria.model: The shared delivery ledger suppresses repeated delivery of the same fact within a session epoch across turns and simultaneous workers.
proposedCriteria.driftMarkers: A same-fact repeat is delivered twice in one session epoch, including across a new turn or concurrent workers, or one session suppresses a different session's eligible fact.
proposedCriteria.method: Run the bound suites through testing:run and require the real-database cases 'a new turn restores spend but only compaction makes the same fact eligible again' and 'dedupes concurrent same-fact attempts and enforces RLS on the real app role'. Preserve first nonempty delivery, zero same-epoch repeats, concurrent one-row outcome, separate-owner control and compaction epoch change. Compaction may re-derive a fresh fact from the current snapshot; it must not replay stale stored text. Missing positive or repeat control rates unknown.

proposedCriteria.title: Push evidence carries current snapshot identity
proposedCriteria.model: Each issued code-intelligence push identifies its snapshot source and refuses stale, foreign or source-drifted evidence as current.
proposedCriteria.driftMarkers: A delivered push lacks its snapshot SHA stamp, serves stale or foreign snapshot content, or labels changed source evidence as current.
proposedCriteria.method: Run the bound suites through testing:run. Require a nonempty real ledger delivery containing 'Snapshot' and its exact commit; exercise stale/future/foreign snapshot rejection and changed definition/caller source-hash controls. Inspect the rendering and validation writers rather than infer currentness from a field name. Source-drift controls must suppress or explicitly qualify the evidence; no cold fallback may disguise a stale snapshot as current. Record exact snapshot SHA and source hashes; absent evidence is unknown.

proposedCriteria.title: Judges can read native code intelligence
proposedCriteria.model: The deployed release operator admits the judge principal to native read-only code-intelligence tools while denying source changes.
proposedCriteria.driftMarkers: On the deployed release operator, judge access to lsp:query, graph:query, code:pack or code:structural is refused by role or capability, or the judge principal receives intel:write needed by lsp:apply.
proposedCriteria.method: Retain the unit detector: run role-principal-caps.test.ts through testing:run and require 'judge can read rubric docs and use read-only SQL/LSP evidence fallbacks without write access'. Check both role allowlists and intel:read capability for lsp:query, graph:query, code:pack and code:structural. The negative requires lsp:apply to need intel:write and that capability to remain absent for judge. Separately verify the actual deployed release-operator artifact with an authenticated signed judge principal: record its serving health/build SHA, effective role/capability identity, exact requests and responses, and invocation-ledger references for nonempty scoped read fixtures through all four read tools. Exercise the denied-write admission control with no source mutation. The release artifact must contain the intended P040 access change, and the source fixture must have a known nonempty answer. Refused reads or an admitted write fails. Missing artifact/identity/read/negative-control evidence is unknown, never pass. A current-build or tree-only journey cannot discharge this final deployed admission guarantee; it remains useful implementation evidence.
